meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law derived from the Civil Code of Québec; federal common law for criminal, regulatory and AML; statutory commercial law)

Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c.17 and regulations thereunder, including the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c.C-46; Quebec: Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (ALPE), CQLR c P-44.1, and Regulation respecting the register of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r.1, ss. 1-92; Code of Civil Procedure for Québec; limited partnership trust and constructive ownership rules under the Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236-2245.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Global Affairs Canada or competent authority in the country of issuance; alternatively, consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Corporate GP or Sponsor)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the country of incorporation of the corporate general partner or institutional investor

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all limited partners, general partners, UBOs and senior agents against: (i) the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and Public Safety Canada's Economic Sanctions Lists; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the Global Affairs Canada Import/Export Control List and pursuant regulations; (iv) the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for any USD clearing or US payment rails; and (v) domestic Canadian police and FINTRAC criminal intelligence databases. The prescribed screening must be conducted at onboarding, at each material change, and on a rolling 30-day basis to identify any new PEP or sanctioned linkage.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Online Services Portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed limited partnership name must be in French or accompany a French version for registration. Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11) and ALPE s.14, non-French words or transliterations are accepted only where a recognized French equivalent does not exist or where the name is a registered trademark. The name must be written in Latin characters; a non-Latin name must be transliterated phonetically into Latin characters and then rendered in French.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is refused, the applicant must review the REQ's written objection reasons and may request an internal review by the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the refusal under ALPE ss. 27.1-29. If internally refused or affirmed, the applicant may appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Québec (Tribunal administratif du Québec) within 30 days of the internal review decision. A brand-new submission with a materially different name is recommended as a parallel contingency to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is conditionally permissible in Québec for the limited partnership's registered office and service of process. However, the limited partnership must establish a physical and operational establishment in Québec, with attributable professional personnel, to satisfy Transport Canada's commercial marine and crew licensing requirements and the CNESST labour obligations. For ISIC 5222 crew recruitment, the registraire requires a verifiable street address (not a speed-mail or telephone answering service) for the individual agent for service of process and for maintaining statutory records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified likelihood of 28% annually for an unannounced on-site inspection in the first fiscal year, rising to 52% by the third year if the venture holds a Transport Canada crewing certificate or registers foreign seafarer placements. Inspections are typically coordinated by the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST), the Registraire des entreprises between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time, and in maritime records audits by Transport Canada.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c CCQ-1991, arts. 2236-2248 (limited partnership / société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, ss. 20-26 (mandatory declaration of registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) of a limited partnership filed with the Registraire des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account is required for a Quebec limited partnership. A limited partner must contribute money or property, not services, and such contribution must be recorded in the partnership records and maintained until redemption or dissolution; the general partner has unlimited liability.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the capital contribution subscriptions of the initial limited partners be and are hereby accepted, and each subscriber shall be admitted upon wiring its subscribed contribution to the Partnership's bank account. FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered office is established at 1250 Boulevard René-Lévesque Ouest, Montréal, Québec H3B 4W8, Canada, and the Registraire des entreprises is instructed to file the Declaration of Registration. FURTHER RESOLVED: That [Name] is appointed General Manager and Compliance Officer, and [Name] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer, each authorized to execute banking, licensing, immigration, and tax documents and to appoint and remove agents for service. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Distinctiveness Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online NUANS name search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS-style name search through the Registraire's official portal to verify that no conflicting enterprise name exists. Select a legal name that includes 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' for the partnership. The Registraire uses the search report to assess distinctive character and comply with Quebec language rules; the name is not formally reserved for partnerships, so proceed to filing promptly after obtaining a clear report.
required_dossiers: Proposed names in priority order
NUANS search report request
Proof of identity of the general partner and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as non-distinctive or non-compliant, select a revised name and obtain a new NUANS report; a request for administrative review may be filed under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal legal counsel / notary in Quebec (private agreement, not filed with the Registrar)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the limited partnership agreement, including contributions of limited partners, profit and loss sharing, management authority reserved to the general partner, transfer restrictions, withdrawal and dissolution clauses, and an express prohibition on limited partners participating in management. Have the general partner execute the agreement and the limited partners execute a contribution schedule. Notarization is not mandatory unless the partnership will acquire immovable property.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement
Capital contribution schedule and subscription letters
Consent and authorization resolution of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the agreement by supplemental deed or a formal ratification resolution if the Registrar, bank, or tax authority queries the terms or if a partner's consent is defective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Registraire's online portal, select 'société en commandite', and complete the Declaration of Registration with the legal name, head office address, first establishment date, principal activity (ISIC 5222 / NAICS 488390), general partner's identity, and the agent for service of process domiciled in Quebec. Submit electronically using the general partner's Quebec access account or an authorized mandatary, and pay the prescribed fee. The certificate of registration and Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) are issued after review.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration
NUANS report
Proof of identity of the filing representative
General partner's written authorization
Power of attorney if filing through a mandatary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried, amend it online or file an application for rectification; provide the requested clarifications within the stated statutory period, and if refused, appeal to the Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Adoption and Agent for Service Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec / internal management
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the registered office is a real and open place in Quebec where documents may be served. Confirm the lease or occupancy right and record the agent for service of process, if any, with the Registrar. Display the registered name at the place of business and maintain records at the head office. Any later change of registered office or agent must be filed as an amendment before the effective date.
required_dossiers: Registered office lease or landlord consent
Agent for service acceptance letter
Proof of occupancy or municipal occupation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the appointed agent declines or is removed, appoint another person domiciled in Quebec and file an amendment with the Registrar without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Quebec Tax Registration and Business Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the NEQ is issued, use the CRA Business Registration Online service to obtain or activate the federal Business Number and any required GST/HST account, unless the partnership qualifies as a small supplier under the Excise Tax Act. Register with Revenu Québec for the Quebec QST and employer source deductions, and complete the partnership information return obligation for the pass-through entity. Provide partner schedules and confirm the general partner's responsibility for tax filings.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from the Registraire
Limited partnership agreement
General partner's business identity details
Names, addresses, and tax identifiers of all partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or Revenu Québec requests additional structural information, file a written explanation with the partnership agreement and partner schedules, and use the 'Authorize a Representative' service to correct any mismatched identity data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Payroll Infrastructure Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian Chartered Bank; CRA Payroll Account; Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the certificate of registration, limited partnership agreement, general partner resolution, and beneficial ownership information to a Canadian bank. Open a multi-currency operating account capable of receiving SWIFT wire transfers in support of seafarer payroll. Register the partnership as an employer with CRA and Revenu Québec, obtain a payroll account, and set up source deduction remittances and T4/T5018 reporting protocols.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration (NEQ)
Limited partnership agreement
General partner resolution on banking mandate
Beneficial ownership and signatory identification documents
Partnership tax registration confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank's customer due diligence process queries beneficial ownership or source of funds, provide a documented ownership chart, partnership agreement, and funding evidence; supplement with a legal opinion if the bank's compliance department requires it.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Publication, Records, and Annual Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the Registrar has published the declaration and that the certificate of registration is displayed or readily available at the registered office. Confirm that the partnership registers its annual update and any subsequent amendments within the time prescribed by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Preserve accounting records, minute/decision books, and contribution records at the head office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration
Annual update acknowledgement from the Registrar
Partnership records and register of partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published particulars are erroneous, apply to the Registrar for rectification and supply supporting evidence; if an annual update is missed, pay the late fee and file the update with a written explanation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) – Licensing Branch for Employment Placement and Recruitment Agencies; Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC) for foreign seafarer recruitment and Labour Market Impact Assessment requirements
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence d'agence de placement et de recrutement de personnel (Employment and Recruitment Agency Licence) issued by CNESST; a Labour Market Impact Assessment or federal authorization may be required for recruitment of foreign crew members

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for office-only maritime crew recruitment operations; no full EIA report or certificate of authorization required under section 31 of the Quebec Environment Quality Act for purely administrative and staffing activities. If vessel mooring or dispatch facilities are later added, a separate environmental authorization review may be triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: For the office occupancy, wastewater must be discharged to municipal sewers in compliance with municipal by-laws; no industrial process wastewater or significant air emissions are generated. Electronic waste, batteries, and office hazardous materials must be recovered or disposed of through permitted recyclers; volatile organic compound emissions from office operations remain within occupational exposure limits and negligible environmental thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and building occupancy approval are required from the municipal fire prevention service and the Régie du bâtiment du Québec, attesting compliance with the National Building Code and Quebec Fire Safety Code for office use. The registered office interior must receive any required structural load inspection for file storage and personnel occupancy. The partnership must register with CNESST as an employer and implement a workplace prevention program, first aid requirements, and an occupational health and safety committee where the workforce size exceeds the statutory trigger.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO) / My Business Account portal; and Revenu Québec (RQ) - CLIC portal for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and provincial employer/payroll accounts. Quebec administers its own provincial VAT (QST) outside the federal Harmonized Sales Tax system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the limited partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) to obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ); 2) Open a CRA Business Number (BN) with the required program accounts (RC for GST/HST, RP for payroll, RT for income tax reference) via BRO or Form RC1; foreign partnerships without a Canadian establishment register through an authorized representative using Form RC59; 3) Register with Revenu Québec for QST (QST registration is conditional on prior GST/HST registration), the QPIP source-deduction account, and CNESST work-assessment coverage if the agency maintains a Quebec establishment or pays Quebec-based crew; 4) Because the LP is fiscally transparent for income tax, no separate corporate income-tax TIN is issued to the partnership; the partnership files annual information returns (T5013 and TP-600) and each partner uses its own domestic tax identification number, supplemented by a Canadian BN when the partner is required to file a Canadian return. Non-resident partners may be subject to Part XIII or section 116 withholding on Canadian-source amounts.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - Under the Income Tax Act (section 96) and the Quebec Taxation Act (section 599), the limited partnership is fiscally transparent: income, losses, and tax credits flow through to partners in proportion to their partnership interests. The partnership is, however, a separate person for GST/HST and QST purposes and must register, collect, and remit indirect taxes independently.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate an IRS-style check-the-box election; partnership transparency is mandatory. Relevant elections available to a Quebec LP: (i) partnership fiscal-period election (ITA s. 249.1 and QTA counterpart) to align or select a non-calendar year-end; (ii) agent/principal GST/HST election under ETA section 211 and the mirror Quebec election; (iii) closely related persons election under ETA section 174 and QSTA section 173 to zero-rate supplies of movable property between affiliates; (iv) EIFEL group/co-designation elections under the Excessive Interest and Financing Expenses Limitation rules applying to cross-border partnerships from 2024; (v) optional annual, quarterly, or installment GST/HST and QST filing elections; (vi) for non-resident partners, elections under ITA section 216 and Part XIII withholding variations to reduce or eliminate Canadian withholding on maritime or leasing income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal Goods and Services Tax at 5%) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST at 9.975% administered by Revenu Québec) - a creditable provincial VAT applied to most supplies of property and services made in Quebec; the combined headline liability borne by an unregistered recipient is 14.975%.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: C$30,000 per four consecutive calendar quarters (the general 'small supplier' threshold) for both GST/HST (ETA s. 148) and QST (QSTA s. 16). Registration becomes mandatory once taxable supplies made in Canada exceed C$30,000. A nil threshold applies to certain non-resident suppliers of telecommunication or courier services, and a special worldwide-revenue test applies to non-resident persons carrying on business in Canada. Voluntary registration is available once the partnership has begun carrying on a business in Canada.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada operates a periodic self-assessed VAT return model (GST34 for GST/HST and VDZ-1 for QST) with no national real-time fiscal clearance, no Continuous Transaction Control (CTC) mandate, and no mandatory digital stamping. E-invoicing is voluntary; PEPPOL and EDI formats are permitted. Invoices must nevertheless contain the prescribed disclosure elements under ETA Schedule V and QSTA section 226, and if books are kept electronically, the underlying records must be retained in an electronically readable format. Revenu Québec requires electronic filing of QST returns and remittance schedules for large registrants via CLIC, and the CRA mandates electronic funds transfer for remittances exceeding C$50,000.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Crew recruitment and vessel crew-management services may be zero-rated as supplies made to non-residents under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act and under the mirror provisions of the QSTA (Schedule II, Part I) if: (i) the recipient is a non-resident shipowner, ship manager, or charterer; (ii) the service is not in respect of real property situated in Canada and not in respect of tangible personal property located in Canada - crew placement for international voyages normally meets this condition because the vessel operates in global waterborne trade; (iii) the non-resident recipient does not carry on a business in Canada with respect to that service; and (iv) the recipient is not registered for GST/HST in respect of the supply. In addition, the agency commission may be zero-rated under the international commercial transportation service provisions (Schedule VI sections 13-15) where the crewing service is integral to an international outbound freight or passenger voyage. The agency must obtain and retain contemporaneous documentary evidence of the counterparty's non-resident status before the consideration becomes due.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / CAED) for any physical export of goods or ship stores, retained where tangible property leaves Canada
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill naming the chartered vessel and the foreign owner or operator
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing the foreign-currency conversion and receipt of export proceeds from a non-resident bank account
Commercial service invoice and executed Crewing Agreement identifying the non-resident vessel principal and the international voyage
Crew manifest or seafarer rosters confirming the service was rendered on an international voyage beyond Canadian territorial waters
Signed statutory declaration of the non-resident status and non-registration of the recipient, supporting the zero-rating claim
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to heightened audit scrutiny by the CRA and Revenu Québec through bank-record cross-checks, counterparty corporate searches, and treaty information exchanges. Although Canada has no statutory exchange-control regime, the 180-day inward-remittance benchmark is the standard documentary expectation; failure to evidence repatriation of export consideration within 180 days will trigger audit red flags and possible denial of zero-rating. The normal reassessment window is four years, but misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud extends the period indefinitely. Upon disallowance, the agency is assessed for uncollected GST (5%) and QST (9.975%) with statutory interest, plus: (i) failure-to-remit penalties under ETA section 280 at 6%-8% of the shortfall (minimum C$250 or C$1,000 for corporations and trusts); (ii) false-statements penalties under ETA section 285 and the parallel Quebec provision of 25% of the unreported tax; (iii) a 50% gross-negligence penalty under ETA section 280.1 for knowingly making false statements; and (iv) criminal prosecution under ETA section 327 and QSTA section 93 for fraudulent evasion, with fines up to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of up to five years. Clawbacks may also extend to the GST/QST input tax credits previously claimed on related expenses, and responsible directors, partners, or promoters may face joint and several liability.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); the Bank acts as fiscal agent for the Government of Canada's Exchange Fund Account and oversees key payment and settlement systems. Canada does not maintain a dedicated foreign-exchange control administration; the Department of Finance exercises overall foreign-exchange policy authority, OSFI prudentially supervises federal banks, and FINTRAC administers AML and electronic-funds-transfer reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada observes full convertibility on both current and capital accounts under IMF Article VIII and imposes no prior approval requirement for capital subscription, foreign loans, dividend payments, or partnership distributions. A Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) may receive inbound capital and repatriate surplus to non-resident partners without Bank of Canada approval. The principal compliance hurdles are tax-related: remittances to non-residents may attract Canadian Part XIII withholding when characterized as interest, dividends, rent, royalties, or management fees; Canadian partnership income allocated to non-resident partners must be reported through T5013 partnership returns and applicable Quebec non-resident forms; treaty relief must be documented. These are tax clearance hurdles, not foreign-exchange restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion rules in Canada. Export and service receipts, including ship-crew recruitment and management fees, may be retained in CAD or any foreign currency for an unlimited period; no percentage of proceeds must be converted into CAD. Reporting obligations are limited to financial-transaction reports: financial institutions must report international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC, and Statistics Canada/Bank of Canada may collect balance-of-payments survey data on cross-border service receipts. No surrender certificate or exchange-control approval is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary settlement bank, MEDIUM as a non-core ancillary payment rail. Offshore digital EMIs may not take deposits or open Canadian-listed bank accounts without authorization under the Bank Act; they may only provide money-transfer services if registered as a FINTRAC money services business and, where applicable, licensed under Quebec's Act respecting money-services businesses. Such accounts are not CDIC-insured and are generally unacceptable for capital escrow, crew payroll trust, or SWIFT-backed commercial settlement. Use EMIs only for pre-funded vendor disbursements or small operational allowances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A limited partnership has no directors; onboarding requires authorized signing officers of the general partner. Physical branch presence is the prevailing norm for a Quebec société en commandite, although remote video onboarding may be permitted where the bank applies an enhanced FINTRAC-compliant non-face-to-face identity verification process. At least one general-partner representative or an appointed Canadian-resident authorized signatory should normally appear in person with original government-issued identification. Foreign signatories may be accommodated with notarized and apostilled documentation, a bank-approved professional referee, or legal counsel confirmation; pure digital remote opening is not guaranteed by Schedule I banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership and inability to identify the ultimate controlling minds of the limited partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified registration excerpt from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; executed limited partnership agreement and all amendments; complete partner register with full legal name, date of birth, residence, ownership percentage and control description; UBO analysis for each partner; if the general partner is a corporation, its register of directors, ultimate shareholders and good-standing certificates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face or incomplete identification of a foreign general partner or remote authorized signatory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport or government-issued ID of each signatory; original or notarized power of attorney / general-partner resolution appointing signatories; certified English/French translations; apostilled corporate documentation; enhanced eKYC video interview record; bank-accepted identity attestation by a regulated professional.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual updating declaration for the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after the end of the limited partnership's financial year; confirm the applicable filing period shown in the enterprise register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may generate prescribed administrative charges and compliance notices. Persistent non-filing may result in cancellation of the partnership's registration after the applicable statutory process, commonly following two consecutive missed annual declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return, where filing conditions are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a December 31 year-end, generally May 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties may apply, including penalties based on the number of partners and days outstanding. Repeated non-compliance may trigger information requests, compliance audits, and partner-level reassessments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: TP-600 Partnership Information Return, where Quebec filing conditions are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties and interest may apply. Revenu Québec may issue compliance notices, assess partners using available information, and impose additional penalties for continued non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general Quebec statutory audit requirement applies solely because the entity is a limited partnership. An independent audit may be required by the partnership agreement, a lender, an investor, a securities-law obligation, a regulated activity, or a contractual reporting requirement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian accounting standards for private enterprises under Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook are generally applicable. IFRS may be used where required or elected, particularly for publicly accountable entities or contractual reporting purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The partnership must maintain and report ultimate beneficial ownership information required under Quebec enterprise-register rules. The annual updating declaration must confirm or update the reported information, and changes to registrable information must generally be filed within 30 days. Transfers of partnership interests must be reflected in the partnership register, ownership records, and beneficial-ownership filings where they alter control or ultimate beneficial ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners and partnership interests
Register of general and limited partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-1,200 annually for a Quebec registered office and administrative filing service, depending on provider and service scope.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-12,000 for an independent audit of a small private limited partnership; no audit fee applies where no audit is required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal general corporate rate 15% plus Quebec general rate 11.5% = combined 26.5% headline. As a Quebec limited partnership, the CA_LP is fiscally transparent: income is allocated to the partners and taxed at the partner level; the LP itself pays no entity-level income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction: qualifying Canadian-controlled corporate partners may claim the C$500,000 active-business limit at a 9% federal rate; the Quebec small business deduction reduces the provincial rate on the eligible C$500,000 allocation. Additional incentives: investment tax credits, scientific research and experimental development credits, and targeted Quebec maritime/port credits (subject to eligibility); GST/HST and QST input tax refunds for registered crewing agencies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (CRA) plus RL-27 slips (Revenu Quebec); filed via CRA EFILE/XML web transmission and Revenu Quebec CLIC/EDI portals.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after partnership fiscal year-end (May 31 for a December 31 year-end); partner statements must be issued by March 31 (or the later of March 31 and the last day of the first month after the fiscal period end).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the partnership BN (9-digit number with RC account) registered with CRA and Revenu Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The general partner must register the LP's BN before filing; a non-resident partner must not substitute its own BN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocate net business income, property income, taxable capital gains, and deductible expenses to each partner in the agreed profit-sharing ratio; ensure total allocations equal partnership net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Segregate the Canadian-source business income attributable to the non-resident partner; state whether the allocation will be reported under Part I and confirm no Part XIII withholding applies to ordinary income draws.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record each partner's country of residence and percentage interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach to the file a valid foreign tax residency certificate and CRA Form NR301 for each non-resident partner claiming treaty benefits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal penalty: C$25 per day for late T5013 filing up to C$2,500 per return; repeat or wilful failures may be prosecuted as an offence under ITA s. 238/239. Quebec penalties mirror the federal amount and are imposed by Revenu Quebec for late or incomplete partnership declarations.
